stem: A body covered a distance of 5 m along a semicircular path. The ratio of distance to displacement is: (A) 11 : 7 (B) 12 : 5 (C) 8 : 3 (D) 7 : 5
An object starts with u = 10 m/s and reaches v = 30 m/s in 10 s. Find acceleration. (A) 1 m/s² (B) 2 m/s² (C) 3 m/s² (D) 4 m/s²

Two balls are dropped to the ground from different heights. One ball is dropped 2 s after the other but they both strike the ground at the same time. If the first ball takes 5 s to reach the ground, then the difference in initial heights is: (Take g = 10 ms⁻²) (A) 20 m (B) 80 m (C) 170 m (D) 40 m

From the top of the tower, a ball A is dropped and another ball B is thrown horizontally at the same time. Which ball strikes the ground first? (A) A (B) B (C) simultaneously (D) depends on the masses
A particle's position as a function of time is described as y(t) = 2t² + 3t + 4. What is the average velocity of the particle from t = 0 to t = 3 sec? (A) 3 m/s (B) 6 m/s (C) 9 m/s (D) 12 m/s

The velocity–time graph of a body moving in a straight line is shown in the figure (v = +4 m/s for 0–2 s, v = −2 m/s for 2–4 s, v = +2 m/s for 4–6 s). The displacement and distance travelled by the body in 6 s are respectively. (A) 8 m, 16 m (B) 16 m, 32 m (C) 16 m, 16 m (D) 8 m, 18 m

An arrow is shot into the air. Its range is 200 metres and its time of flight is 5 sec. If the value of g is assumed to be 10 m/sec². What is the angle of projection with the horizontal: (A) tan⁻¹(4/5) (B) tan⁻¹(5/4) (C) tan⁻¹(5/8) (D) tan⁻¹(8/5)

A river of width 500 m has flow velocity 3 m/s. A man starts swimming perpendicular to river flow at a speed of 4 m/s relative to water. Simultaneously a car starts moving on a road, that runs along the opposite side of the river, with constant speed. The car starts from a point on the other side that is exactly opposite to the point from where the man starts swimming. The speed of the car if both, the car and the man, meet at the same point at the moment man has crossed the river, is: (in m/s) (A) 3 (B) 4 (C) 5 (D) none of these

Three particles start from origin at the same time with a velocity 2 ms⁻¹ along positive x-axis, the second with a velocity 6 ms⁻¹ along negative y-axis. Find the velocity of the third particle along x = y line so that the three particles may always lie in a straight line (A) −3√3 (B) 3√2 (C) −3√2 (D) 2√2

A body A is thrown vertically upwards with such a velocity that it reaches a maximum height of h. Simultaneously another body B is dropped from height h. It strikes the ground and does not rebound. The velocity of A relative to B v/s time graph is best represented by: (upward direction is positive) (A) straight line falling to zero (B) V-shaped (C) constant, then falling after B lands (D) zero then rising

Two tall buildings are 30 m apart. The speed with which a ball must be thrown horizontally from a window 150 m above the ground in one building so that it enters a window 27.5 m from the ground in the other building is: (A) 2 ms⁻¹ (B) 6 ms⁻¹ (C) 4 ms⁻¹ (D) 8 ms⁻¹

A particle starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration. The ratio of distance covered in the 5th second to the total distance covered in the first 5 seconds is: (A) 9/25 (B) 5/9 (C) 9/14 (D) 10/9

A particle moves along a straight line OX. At a time t (in seconds) the position x (in metres) of the particle from O is given by: x = 40 + 12t − t³. How long (in m) would the particle travel before coming to rest? (A) 16 m (B) 24 m (C) 40 m (D) 56 m
A particle is moving along the x-axis whose instantaneous speed is given by v² = 108 − 9x². The acceleration of the particle is (A) −9x ms⁻² (B) −18x ms⁻² (C) (−9x/2) ms⁻² (D) none of these

A particle is projected with velocity V₀ along x-axis. The deceleration on the particle is proportional to the square of the distance from the origin i.e. a = −αx², the distance at which the particle stops is (A) √(3V₀/2α) (B) (3V₀/2α)^(1/3) (C) √(2V₀²/3α) (D) (3V₀²/2α)^(1/3)

The fig. shows position–time graph of two riders C and D (both straight lines, intersecting at t = 10 s; C steeper than D). Based on the information represented by the graph, at t = 10 s: (A) C and D are at the same position (B) C and D have the same velocity (C) The velocity of D is greater than the velocity of C (D) C is in front of D

A lift is moving with a uniform downward acceleration of 2 m/s². A ball is dropped from a height 2 m from the floor of lift. Find the time taken after which ball will strike the floor? (Take g = 10 m/s²) (A) √2 sec (B) 2 sec (C) 1/2 sec (D) 1/√2 sec

Two particles P and Q are initially 40 m apart, P behind Q. Particle P starts moving with a uniform velocity 10 m/s towards Q. Particle Q starting from rest has an acceleration 2 m/s² in the direction of velocity of P. Then the minimum distance between P and Q will be (A) 45 m (B) 15 m (C) 35 m (D) 30 m

A thief is running away on a straight road in a jeep moving with a speed of 9 ms⁻¹. A policeman chases him on a motor cycle moving at a speed of 10 ms⁻¹. If the instantaneous separation of the jeep from the motor cycle is 100 m, how long will it take for the policeman to catch the thief? (A) 1 s (B) 19 s (C) 90 s (D) 100 s

A girl standing on road holds her umbrella at 37° with the vertical to keep the rain away. If she starts running without umbrella with a speed of 15√2 kmh⁻¹, the rain drops hit her head vertically. The speed of rain drops with respect to the moving girl is: (A) 30 kmh⁻¹ (B) 20√2 kmh⁻¹ (C) 30/√2 kmh⁻¹ (D) 25 kmh⁻¹
A bird flies for 4 s with a velocity v = (t − 2) m/s in a straight line, where t = time in second. Calculate the distance covered by the bird in meter.

A body is projected with a velocity v₁ from the point A at 30° to the horizontal. At the same time, another body is projected vertically upwards from B with velocity v₂. The point B lies vertically below the highest point. For both the bodies to collide, v₂/v₁ should be 1/x, then x = ______.
The velocity of a projectile when it is at the greatest height is √(2/5) times its velocity when it is at half of its greatest height. Determine its angle of projection in degree.

A projectile is thrown with velocity v making an angle θ with the horizontal. It just crosses the top of two poles, each of height h, after 1 second and 3 second respectively. The time of flight (in sec) of the projectile is
An object moving with a speed of 6.25 m/s, is decelerated at a rate given by dv/dt = −2.5√v where v is the instantaneous speed. The time (in s) taken by the object, to come to rest, would be

A particle has a velocity u towards east at t = 0. Its acceleration is towards west and is constant. Let x A and x B be the magnitudes of displacements in the first 10 seconds and the next 10 seconds. (A) x A < x B (B) x A = x B (C) x A > x B (D) the information is insufficient to decide the relation of x A with x B

A river is flowing from west to east at a speed of 5 metres per minute. A man on the south bank of the river, capable of swimming at 10 metres per minute in still water, wants to swim across the river in the shortest time. He should swim in a direction (A) due north (B) 30° east of north (C) 30° north of west (D) 60° east of north

key: A triangle peaking at 6 m/s at t = 2 s
stem: A particle starts from rest at t = 0 and undergoes an acceleration a (in m s −2 ) with time t in seconds as shown: a = +3 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 2, then a = −3 for 2 ≤ t ≤ 4. Which plot represents velocity v versus time t? (A) triangle rising to 6 at t = 2 and back to 0 at t = 4 (B) straight line rising to 6 at t = 4 (C) step graph 4 then −4 (D) line falling from 4 to 2

One body is dropped while a second body is thrown downwards with an initial velocity of 2 m/s simultaneously. The separation between them is 18 metres after a time: (A) 9 s (B) 4.5 s (C) 18 s (D) 9.8 s
A point moves in a straight line so that its displacement x m at time t sec is given by x² = 1 + t². Its acceleration in m/sec² at a time t sec is: (A) 1/x² (B) −t/x³ (C) 1/x − t²/x³ (D) 1/x − 1/x²

The graph describes an airplane’s acceleration during its take-off run: a rises linearly from 3 to 5 m s −2 over 0–10 s, then stays at 5 m s −2 from 10–20 s. The airplane’s velocity when it lifts off at t = 20 s is: (A) 40 m s −1 (B) 50 m s −1 (C) 90 m s −1 (D) 180 m s −1

A particle is projected with velocity v 0 along the x-axis. The deceleration on the particle is proportional to the square of the distance from the origin, i.e. a = −αx². The distance at which the particle stops is: (A) √(3v 0 /2α) (B) (3v 0 /2α) 1/3 (C) √(2v 0 ²/3α) (D) (3v 0 ²/2α) 1/3

Two particles A and B start from the same point and move in the positive x-direction. In a time interval of 2.00 s after they start, their velocities v vary with time t as shown: A holds 2.00 m/s for the first second then 1.00 m/s for the second; B is a sawtooth rising linearly 0 → 2.00 m/s over each one-second interval. What is the maximum separation between the particles during this time interval? (A) 1.00 m (B) 1.25 m (C) 1.50 m (D) 2.00 m

When a car passes mark-A, the driver applies brakes. Thereafter, reducing speed uniformly from 160 km/h at A, the car passes mark C with a speed of 40 km/h. The marks are at equal distances on the road. Where on the road was the car moving with a speed of 100 km/h? (A) At mark-B (B) Between mark-A and mark-B (C) Between mark-B and mark-C (D) Information is insufficient to decide.

In the arrangement of rigid links of equal length l, they can freely rotate about the joined ends as shown. If the end U is pulled horizontally with constant speed 20 m/s, find the approximate speed of end P when the angle SUT is 90°. (A) 5 m/s (B) 10 m/s (C) 7.1 m/s (D) 14.12 m/s
A person travelling at 43.2 km/h applies the brake giving a deceleration of 6.0 m/s² to his scooter. How far (in m) will it travel before stopping? (A) 10 (B) 12 (C) 14 (D) 16

A small sphere is projected with a velocity of 3 m s −1 in a direction 60° from the horizontal y-axis, on a smooth inclined plane of inclination 30°. The motion of the sphere takes place in the x-y plane of the incline. Calculate the magnitude “2v” (in m s −1 ) of its velocity after 2 s.

Figure shows an enemy tank moving with a speed of 9 m/s in the direction shown. A gun can fire shells in the y-z plane only, with a speed of 100 m/s at an angle of 53°. The tank is initially at a perpendicular distance of 360 m from the plane of firing. If the tank started at t = 0, then the time interval (in sec) after which the shell is to be fired to hit the tank?
A particle starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. Then the ratio of distance covered in n th second to n seconds is (A) n²/(2n − 1) (B) 2/n − 1/n² (C) n²/(n + 1) (D) (2n + 1)/n²

A particle “P” moves with constant velocity u along the x-axis. Q always has velocity towards P. If Q moves with constant speed V (initially Q is a distance l directly below P, moving towards it), then distance travelled by Q before meeting is ____ (A) uVl/√(V² − u²) (B) V²l/(V² − u²) (C) V²/(V² − u²) (D) lu/(V² − u²)

Find time of flight and range of the projectile along the inclined plane as shown in figure (plane inclined at 30°; particle projected from a point on the plane at 20√2 m/s, at 45° above the horizontal, towards the lower side of the incline). (g = 10 m/s²) (A) 145.71 m (B) 165.71 m (C) 185.71 m (D) None of these

An object moving with a speed of 6.25 m/s, is decelerated at a rate given by dv/dt = −2.5√v where ‘v’ is the instantaneous speed. The time taken by the object, to come to rest, would be (A) 1 s (B) 2 s (C) 4 s (D) 8 s

The particle A is projected from point P with velocity ‘u’ along the (smooth) plane and simultaneously another particle B with velocity ‘v’ at an angle ‘α’ with vertical. The particles collide at point Q on the plane (plane inclined at θ to the horizontal). Then: (A) −v sin(θ − α) = u (B) v cos(θ − α) = u (C) v = u (D) tan(θ − α) = u

Three walls of height h, H, h are at equal distances ‘a’ apart. A ball is thrown in a vertical plane perpendicular to the wall so that it just clears all the walls. The ball strikes the ground at a distance x from the middle wall, then x = : (A) 4a (B) 2a (C) 2a√(H/(H − h)) (D) a√(H/(H − h))

Three particles start from the origin at the same time, one with a velocity V 1 along x-axis, the second along the y-axis with velocity V 2 and the third along x = y line. The velocity of the third so that the three may always lie on the same line is: (A) V 1 V 2 /(V 1 + V 2 ) (B) √2 V 1 V 2 /(V 1 + V 2 ) (C) √3 V 1 V 2 /(V 1 + V 2 ) (D) Zero

The deceleration experienced by a moving motor boat, after its engine is cut-off is given by dv/dt = −kv³, where ‘k’ is constant. If v 0 is the magnitude of the velocity at cut-off, the magnitude of the velocity at a time ‘t’ after the cut-off is (A) v 0 /2 (B) v (C) v 0 e −kt (D) v 0 /√(2v 0 ²kt + 1)

A launch plies between two points A and B on the opposite banks of a river, always following the line AB. The distance S between A and B is 1200 m. The velocity of the river current v = 1.9 m/s is constant over the entire width of the river. The line AB makes an angle α = 60° with the direction of the current. With what velocity u (in m/s) should the launch move to cover the distance AB and back in a time t = 5 min? The angle β (between u and AB) remains the same during the passage from A to B and from B to A.

A body falling freely from a given height H hits an inclined plane in its path at a height h. As a result of this impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. For what value of H/h will the body take maximum time to reach the ground?

A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Assuming the acceleration due to gravity is −9.8 m/s 2 , how high does the ball go before it starts falling back to the ground? (A) 20.41 m (B) 40.41 m (C) 50.41 m (D) 60 m
A particle starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration. Then the ratio of distance covered in n th second to n seconds is (A) n 2 /(2n − 1) (B) 2/n − 1/n 2 (C) n 2 /(n + 1) (D) (2n + 1)/n 2

A train traveling at 90 km/h can decelerate at a constant rate to come to a stop in 30 seconds. What is its deceleration? (A) a = (5/6) m/s 2 (B) a = (5/18) m/s 2 (C) a = (5/20) m/s 2 (D) a = (5/12) m/s 2

A particle is moving eastwards with a velocity 5 ms −1 , changes its direction northwards and moves with same magnitude of velocity. The average acceleration in 10 seconds is (A) zero (B) (1/√2) ms −2 towards N-E (C) (1/√2) ms −2 towards S-E (D) (1/√2) ms −2 towards N-W

A body is projected with a velocity v 1 from the point A as shown in the figure. At the same time, another body is projected vertically upwards from B with velocity v 2 . The point B lies vertically below the highest point. For both the bodies to collide, (v 2 /v 1 )² should be 1/x, then 4x = ______. [Figure: v 1 at 30° to the horizontal at A; B on the same level, directly below the top of the trajectory.]
